key_insight: Conformal prediction turns deterministic neural-operator CFD surrogates into calibrated, reliability-aware tools for both vehicle-level drag and spatial surface-field uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables aerodynamic design teams to prioritize which vehicle geometries, pressure regions, or shear-stress hotspots need high-fidelity CFD verification, reducing wasted simulation effort.
method: Use GeoTransolver as the main neural-operator surrogate and Transolver to test transfer across architectures.
For drag, apply conformalized quantile regression to produce calibrated case-level prediction intervals.
For pressure and wall shear stress, combine point prediction with residual-scale estimation and residual-normalized conformal calibration for spatially adaptive intervals.
evidence_signal: At 90% nominal coverage, out-of-fold calibration reduced drag-coverage variability from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points and cut mean interval width by 22.68% for pressure and 25.35%–27.09% for WSS.
watch_item: Conservative case-wise normalized intervals can improve reliability but may be wider, so practical deployment must balance calibration strength against usable sharpness.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
